title: Execution of a digit increment statement
statement: Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be machine limits, $P$ a program, $d,v_b,v_n,\mathrm{base},n,j\in\mathbb N$, and let $l$ be a list of natural numbers. Let $\mu,\mathrm{loc}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. Suppose the space limit is at most the word limit, $n$ is at most the word limit, $\mathrm{loc}(v_b)=\mathrm{base}$, and $\mathrm{loc}(v_n)=n$. Suppose also that the segment beginning at $\mathrm{base}+j$ with length $|l|$ fits within the space limit, every entry of $l$ is less than $n$, and memory $\mu$ on that segment agrees with the integer-valued list obtained by viewing each entry of $l$ as an integer. Then the statement that increments the digits of this segment has an execution from state $(\mathrm{loc},\mu)$ with cost at most $14|l|+5$ whose final state preserves $\mathrm{loc}$, has the incremented digit list on that segment, and agrees with $\mu$ at every address outside the segment.
hypotheses_covered: Space limit is at most word limit
The segment of length $|l|$ starting at $\mathrm{base}+j$ fits in the space limit
Every entry of $l$ is less than $n$
Initial memory agrees with the integer-valued list $l$ on the segment
